summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease, metastatic rectal adenocarcinoma, and a history of osteosarcoma was admitted for a severe painful crisis triggered by a viral upper respiratory infection and dehydration. She developed community-acquired pneumonia and acute chest syndrome, requiring oxygen, antibiotics, IV fluids, and blood transfusions. Her course was complicated by worsening respiratory status and disseminated intravascular coagulation. On hospital day 23, she experienced an acute mental status change, and imaging revealed a nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage in the setting of coagulopathy. Despite supportive care and neurosurgical consultation, her neurological condition deteriorated. Goals of care were transitioned to comfort measures only after discussions with her family, and she passed away on December 16. Throughout the admission, she remained malnourished and had evidence of acute kidney injury and proteinuria.
